panels.contextImmediatelyAfter: Lala announces the quiz.

panels.currentStoryBeat: Lala cheerfully becomes proctor while Jerry reacts.

panels.contextImmediatelyAfter: Old Du returns to jazz harmony.

panels.contextImmediatelyBefore: Bossa Nova shows another fusion recipe.
panels.currentStoryBeat: Old Du demonstrates a three-step chord path at the piano.
panels.contextImmediatelyAfter: The idea returns to the Hill group.

panels.currentStoryBeat: Jerry and Lala combine electric guitar and violin beside a bamboo flute stand.
panels.contextImmediatelyAfter: The ten-question quiz starts.

panels.contextImmediatelyBefore: Question one asks about the roots of blues.
panels.currentStoryBeat: A respectful wide cotton-field and port image evokes the historical answer.
panels.contextImmediatelyAfter: The explanation connects field hollers to New Orleans.

panels.contextImmediatelyBefore: Question two asks which 1969 album ignited fusion.
panels.currentStoryBeat: A blank deep-blue record sleeve sits beside electric piano and guitar cable.
panels.contextImmediatelyAfter: The answer identifies the electric-jazz turning point.

panels.contextImmediatelyBefore: Question three asks what jazz first fused with.
panels.currentStoryBeat: Saxophone and supported electric guitar meet above amp and drums.
panels.contextImmediatelyAfter: The answer explains jazz meeting rock.

panels.currentStoryBeat: A bird crosses stormy weather above a vintage synthesizer.
panels.contextImmediatelyAfter: The answer names the 1977 album.

panels.contextImmediatelyBefore: Question five asks where Bossa Nova began.
panels.currentStoryBeat: A supported acoustic guitar overlooks a Brazilian seaside promenade.
panels.contextImmediatelyAfter: The answer returns to Rio de Janeiro.

panels.currentStoryBeat: Three blank chord cards form a path above a correct piano keyboard.
panels.contextImmediatelyAfter: The answer explains ii–V–I.

panels.contextImmediatelyBefore: Question seven asks about funk entering jazz.
panels.currentStoryBeat: Clavinet, synthesizer, bass and drums fill a vivid 1970s stage.
panels.contextImmediatelyAfter: The answer names the funk-fusion record.

panels.contextImmediatelyBefore: Question eight asks about Mahavishnu Orchestra.
panels.currentStoryBeat: A supported double-neck guitar meets Indian percussion and abstract rhythm dots.
panels.contextImmediatelyAfter: The answer names the guitarist and Indian influence.

panels.contextImmediatelyBefore: Question nine asks what modal jazz changes.
panels.currentStoryBeat: A sparse blue piano room expresses open harmonic space.
panels.contextImmediatelyAfter: The answer explains fewer chord changes.

panels.contextImmediatelyBefore: Question ten returns to the first night at the Hill.
panels.currentStoryBeat: Jerry separates frequencies at the console while Lala plays violin.
panels.contextImmediatelyAfter: The answer explains making room for strings.

panels.contextImmediatelyBefore: Jerry has answered all ten questions and the score is already known.
panels.currentStoryBeat: Lala reacts to the score with a completely blank result sheet while Old Du rests his intact saxophone across his lap and closes the late-night class.
panels.contextImmediatelyAfter: Old Du tells everyone to go home and not be late for Saturday rehearsal.
